newsitem.title: UK: Hays declines comment on Salvesen talk.
newsitem.headline: Hays declines comment on Salvesen talk.

text.p: British business services company Hays Plc on Friday declined to comment on a newspaper report suggesting it could bid for logistics group Christian Salvesen Plc.
"We never comment on press speculation," Hays' managing director John Napier told Reuters. Salvesen shares had risen 15 pence to 311.5 pence at 0830 GMT.

But market sources said the report, in the Times newspaper, was incorrect to suggest Hays had been frozen out of making a bid for Salvesen by takeover rules for a year and would be free to do so "within a few weeks".

"Hays has been free to make a bid at any time," one industry source said. A City regulatory source confirmed this, pointing out Hays had not at any point made a formal bid for Salvesen but had simply held talks in July last year and agreement was never reached.

If Hays had made a formal offer for Salvesen or denied making a bid for the group, then it would have been frozen out of making another approach for up to a year by the City Code on Takeovers and Mergers.
But this had not been the case and Hays "had not been barred from coming back", the second source said.

Market sources said Salvesen's impending demerger of its Aggreko equipment hire business, which was seen as the star performer of its varied businesses, meant Hays had no interest in bidding for Salvesen.
"Salvesen was never a 'need to do', it was a 'nice to do'," one source said.
Hays shares were down 2.5 pence at 573.5 pence at 0853 GMT.
